evidence_spans.text: The ablation study presented in Table 4 demonstrates that AttentionPert achieves the lowest MSE(DE) in the seen 0/2 scenario, which indicates that the enhanced performance of AttentionPert is not solely attributable to any one of these three changes or their combination. Therefore, the design of AttentionPert is essential for its improved performance.
Results demonstrate that AttentionPert with NA-bias more accurately predicts nonadditive expression changes.

The results presented in Table 5 reveal that while each encoder contributes to the model’s performance, neither encoder individually outperforms the effectiveness of the integrated model that combines both encoders. This underscores the synergistic effect of incorporating both the PertWeight and PertLocal encoders into AttentionPert.

AttentionPert outperforms prior methods including the SOTA GEARS model on RPE1 and K562 datasets (Replogle et al. 2022), each of which comprises >1000 single-gene perturbations, and on the Norman dataset containing 131 two-gene perturbations (Norman et al. 2019).
The results demonstrate that AttentionPert outperforms all baseline models across these scenarios, particularly in the most OOD scenario where both test genes are unseen in the train set.

AttentionPert integrates global and local effects in a multi-scale model, representing both the nonuniform system-wide impact of the genetic perturbation and the localized disturbance in a network of gene–gene similarities, enhancing its ability to predict nuanced transcriptional responses to both single and multi-gene perturbations.

Figure 6 illustrates the ability of AttentionPert to capture the nonadditive nature of multiplexed genetic perturbations. When predicting a seen 2/2 perturbation: FOXA1 and HOXB9, AttentionPert is adept at learning the combined response of these genes. This approach differs markedly from a simple additive model, which merely sums the transcriptional effects of each gene perturbed independently.

Particularly, AttentionPert has exceptional capability in the most challenging out-of-distribution (OOD) task: predicting the effects of novel multi-gene perturbations where none of the perturbed genes have been encountered during the training phase.

methods.description: AttentionPert takes perturbation indicators as input into two modules: PertWeight and PertLocal encoders. Each outputs an encoding matrix (RK×D). The sum is fed into a gene-specific linear decoder to predict the expression shift. The prediction is added to a random control sample. Loss function combines auto-focus and direction-aware loss (GEARS). Hyperparameters: embedding size De=200 (Gene2Vec), SGConv hops t=1, hidden size D=64, attention heads H=2, head dimension dq=dk=dv=64, GO graph edge weight multiplier α=0.75, NA-bias β=0.05, trained for 20 epochs, batch size 128, Adam optimizer with learning rate 1e-3.

methods.description: Embeds genes into weight embedding Ew and pert embedding Ep. Applies four SGConv GNN encoders on the GO graph to produce Q, K, V, P. V is masked by perturbation indicators. Multi-head attention computes weighted global effects, combined with P via addition and feed-forward layers to produce HPW.
